recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed unless maintainers separately decide to regenerate archived tools/history artifacts, which are not current build inputs for this reconciliation.
issue_request: FHIR-39381 is a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core technical correction, raised in R4B and applied for R5, asking the language value set to spell Telugu correctly and to spell Frisian and Frisian (Netherlands) correctly instead of Frysian.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by commit aaa71eaba960fd04f41a483bac5a21543d26245f, which changed source/terminologies/valueset-languages.xml and source/terminologies/valueset-written-languages.xml from Telegu/Frysian to Telugu/Frisian. That implementation is in v5.0.0 history.
additional_context: Current source/terminologies/valueset-languages.xml has Frisian, Frisian (Netherlands), and Telugu for fy, fy-NL, and te. Current source/terminologies/valueset-written-languages.xml also has Frisian and Telugu, and written-languages is active in source/fhir.ini. The Common Languages source remains referenced as the starter binding in source/terminologies/bindings.xml and by current binding links. Searches found no remaining Telegu/Frysian spellings in current source; old spellings remain only in historical generated snapshots under tools/history. A 2016 Zulip Common Languages thread explains where the affected entries came from and contains the old Frysian spelling, but no conflicting later community decision was found.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch because the active current specification sources already reflect the Published Jira correction and no source edit is needed.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive technical correction asking to fix Telegu to Telugu and Frysian/Frysian (Netherlands) to Frisian/Frisian (Netherlands) in the language value set.
evidence_items.learned: This establishes final WG intent and the exact target spellings for reconciliation.

evidence_items.summary: The current Common Languages source displays fy as Frisian, fy-NL as Frisian (Netherlands), and te as Telugu.
evidence_items.learned: The value set named by the Jira related URL already contains the requested corrected English names.

evidence_items.summary: The active written-languages value set source also displays fy as Frisian and te as Telugu, and fhir.ini lists written-languages as an active value set input.
evidence_items.learned: The parallel active source touched by the original application is correct and in build scope.

evidence_items.summary: Commit 'FHIR-39381 Misspelled language names in value set' changed source/terminologies/valueset-languages.xml and source/terminologies/valueset-written-languages.xml from Telegu/Frysian to Telugu/Frisian.
evidence_items.learned: The Jira issue had a direct prior source application before this reconciliation.

evidence_items.summary: The 2016 thread requested translations for valueset-languages.xml, discussed Telugu, and introduced fy/fy-NL with the old Frysian spelling.
evidence_items.learned: This explains the origin of the affected entries but provides no conflicting reason to keep the misspellings.
